question: What agency administers Utah's motorcycle rider training program and motorcycle knowledge testing?
choice_a: The Driver License Division (DLD) of the Utah Department of Public Safety
choice_b: The Utah Division of Motor Vehicles (DMV)
choice_c: The Utah Division of Parks and Recreation
explanation: The manual explains the Utah Motorcycle Rider Training Program is part of the Driver License Division (DLD) of the Department of Public Safety, which administers the statewide rider education program; the DMV is a separate agency handling vehicle/vessel registration.
source_note: Motorcycling in Utah - License; Utah Rider Training Program, UT2, UT19

question: Under Utah law described in the manual, what must a person have in their possession to legally operate a motorcycle on public roads?
choice_a: A separate motorcycle-only license unrelated to any driver license
choice_b: A valid driver license with an endorsement for operating motorcycles
choice_d: No license is required if the rider is over 21
explanation: The manual states Utah law requires everyone operating a motorcycle on Utah public roads and highways to have in their possession a valid driver license with an endorsement for operating motorcycles.

question: What are the minimum requirements to obtain a Utah motorcycle learner permit, per the manual?
choice_a: Hold only a motorcycle learner permit from another state
choice_b: Be at least 14 years old with no other license required
choice_c: Be at least 16 years old, hold a valid Class D or Commercial Driver License, and pass the vision test and required motorcycle written test
choice_d: Be at least 18 with no written test required
explanation: The manual states a temporary learner permit can be issued if the applicant is at least 16 years old, has a valid Class D or Commercial Driver License, and has passed the vision test and the required motorcycle written test.

question: How long is a Utah motorcycle learner permit valid, per the manual?
explanation: The manual states a motorcycle learner permit is valid for six months, obtained by completing the application process and paying the fee at a driver license office.

question: For the first two months after a motorcycle learner permit is issued, which of the following is the permit holder prohibited from doing?
choice_a: Operating on a highway posted at 60 mph or more, carrying passengers, or riding between 10 P.M. and 6 A.M.
choice_c: Riding on any public road under any circumstances
choice_d: Wearing a helmet other than a full-face style
explanation: The manual lists three restrictions for the first two months of a motorcycle learner permit: no highway operation at 60 mph or more, no carrying passengers, and no riding between 10 P.M. and 6 A.M.

question: Under what circumstance can the two-month learner permit restriction period be waived for someone younger than 19, per the manual?
choice_a: It can never be waived regardless of training
choice_b: Upon proof of completion of the Basic Rider Course (BRC)
choice_d: By having a parent co-sign the permit application
explanation: The manual states anyone younger than 19 must hold the motorcycle learner permit for two months, but the requirement may be waived upon proof of completion of the Basic Rider Course (BRC).

question: Under Utah's tiered motorcycle licensing system, what determines the size restriction placed on a rider's endorsement?
choice_a: The size of motorcycle the rider owns, regardless of what they test on
choice_b: The rider's age at the time of application
choice_c: The size of the motorcycle used at the time of the skills test
choice_d: The county where the applicant lives
explanation: The manual explains that under Utah's tiered licensing system, the restriction on a motorcycle endorsement is determined by the size of the motorcycle used at the time of the skills test.
source_note: Motorcycling in Utah - Tiered Licensing, UT3

question: Under Utah's tiered licensing system, what restriction applies if a rider tests on a motorcycle of 650cc or larger?
choice_a: The rider may only ride three-wheeled motorcycles
choice_b: The rider is restricted to 650cc or smaller only
choice_d: The rider will not be restricted
explanation: The manual states that if you test on a motorcycle 650cc or larger, you will not be restricted, whereas testing on smaller motorcycles (90cc, 249cc, or 649cc or less) restricts the rider to that size class or smaller.
source_note: Motorcycling in Utah - Tiered Licensing, UT3

question: If a rider takes the motorcycle skills test on a three-wheeled motorcycle, what restriction applies, per the manual?
choice_a: The rider will be restricted to riding only three-wheeled motorcycles
choice_b: No restriction applies regardless of the vehicle tested on
choice_c: The rider may ride any two-wheel motorcycle without limitation
choice_d: The rider must retest every six months
explanation: The manual notes that if you test on a three-wheeled motorcycle, you will be restricted to riding only three-wheeled motorcycles.
source_note: Motorcycling in Utah - Motorcycle Skill Test, UT5

question: According to the Utah Driver License Division's official website, how many questions are on Utah's motorcycle endorsement written knowledge test?
explanation: Two independent official dld.utah.gov pages (the motorcycle endorsement page and the motorcycle page) both state applicants are 'required to pass a 25-question closed-book test' to obtain the motorcycle endorsement, distinct from the driver knowledge test's 50-question (never licensed) or 25-question open-book (previously licensed) formats.
source_note: dld.utah.gov/add-motorcycle-endorsement/ and dld.utah.gov/motorcycle/, official DLD pages (2026 research)

question: What minimum age and prior licensing requirement does the manual state for applying for a motorcycle endorsement in Utah?
choice_a: At least 14 years of age with parental consent only
choice_b: At least 21 years of age with no other license needed
choice_c: At least 16 years of age and already holding a valid Class D driver license
choice_d: No age requirement, only a completed skills test
explanation: The official dld.utah.gov motorcycle endorsement page states applicants must be at least 16 years of age and hold a valid Class D driver license to apply for a motorcycle endorsement.

question: What is the Basic Rider Course (BRC) described in the manual's Utah Rider Training Program section?
choice_a: A course offered only to CDL holders
choice_b: A one-hour online-only course with no hands-on riding
choice_c: A mandatory 40-hour course required of every licensed rider annually
choice_d: A 15-hour basic course (10 hours of actual riding) teaching physical and mental skills for safe riding, with motorcycles and helmets furnished
explanation: The manual describes the BRC as a 15-hour basic course, including 10 hours of actual riding, teaching physical and mental skills and responsible attitude for safe riding; motorcycles and helmets are furnished, and no previous experience is required.
source_note: Utah Rider Training Program - Basic Rider Course (BRC), UT19

question: What benefit does completing the BRC potentially provide toward a Utah motorcycle endorsement, per the manual?
choice_a: The Driver License Division may waive the skill (road) portion of the motorcycle endorsement tests if applied for within six months of completion
choice_b: It automatically issues an unrestricted endorsement regardless of test motorcycle size
choice_c: It waives the written knowledge test entirely
choice_d: It has no bearing on the endorsement process
explanation: The manual states that if a graduate applies for a motorcycle endorsement within six months after completing the BRC, the DLD may waive the skill (road) portion of the motorcycle endorsement tests.
source_note: Utah Rider Training Program - Basic Rider Course (BRC), UT19

question: What is the Basic Rider Course 2 (BRC2) designed for, per the manual?
choice_a: Complete beginners with no riding experience
choice_b: The experienced rider, teaching risk management, rear-wheel skid control, and hazard avoidance using the rider's own motorcycle
choice_d: Only CDL applicants seeking a motorcycle endorsement
explanation: The manual describes the BRC2 as a five-hour course designed specifically for the experienced rider, covering risk management, rear-wheel skid control, hazard detection/avoidance, and traction management, using the rider's own motorcycle.
source_note: Utah Rider Training Program - Basic Rider Course 2 (BRC2), UT19-20

question: Starting July 1, 2009, what age makes a rider eligible to enroll in an approved Utah rider training course, per the manual?
choice_a: 21 years of age or older only
choice_b: 18 years of age with no other requirement
choice_c: 15 years and six months of age or older, holding a valid learner permit or driver license, or eligible for a motorcycle learner permit
choice_d: There is no minimum age for enrollment
explanation: The manual states that starting July 1, 2009, a person 15 years and six months of age or older who holds a valid learner permit or driver license, or is eligible for a motorcycle learner permit, may enroll in and complete an approved rider training course.
source_note: Utah Rider Training Program - Basic Rider Course (BRC), UT19

question: If a BRC or BRC2 graduate plans to ride a motorcycle greater than 650cc, what does the manual say they must do?
choice_a: Retake the entire BRC course on a larger motorcycle
choice_b: Nothing extra; the BRC waiver covers all motorcycle sizes automatically
choice_c: Wait an additional year before riding any motorcycle over 650cc
choice_d: Either pass the riding skills test with the school or with the DLD using a 650cc or larger motorcycle
explanation: The manual notes that a BRC or BRC2 graduate planning to ride a motorcycle greater than 650cc will need to either pass the riding skills test with the school or with the DLD using a 650cc or larger motorcycle.
source_note: Utah Rider Training Program - Basic Rider Course (BRC), UT20

question: What must an applicant provide for the motorcycle skills test at a Utah driver license office, per the manual?
choice_b: No motorcycle; the office always supplies one
choice_c: Only a valid learner permit, since no motorcycle is used in the skills test
choice_d: A rented motorcycle from an approved vendor list
explanation: The manual states applicants must provide their own motorcycle for the skills test at the driver license office, and skills tests are given by appointment only in most offices.
source_note: Motorcycling in Utah - Motorcycle Skill Test, UT3

question: If a Utah resident has a change of address, how many days does the manual say they have to notify the Driver License Division?
choice_d: There is no requirement to report an address change
explanation: The manual states that if a person has a change of address, they are required by law to notify the division of the new address within ten days, either online or in person with two acceptable proofs of residency.
source_note: Motorcycling in Utah - Traffic Rules and Regulations, UT6
